summary: Checked Tucker and Talbert's f100r claims against the Beinecke scan and filed the one pairing that survives looking: their plant No. 8 (Opuntia, label read as nashtli/nochtli) is the drawing beside the label ZL gives as f100r.8 soity. Their plant numbering is undefined in the article, so I pinned it from the scan: the inline glyph image for their No. 4 name maguoey matches the label ZL gives as f100r.4 chofary in shape and position, so No. N = f100r.N. Against the anchor: the marginal projections are drawn like leaf teeth elsewhere on the page, a pad that tapers into a neck and taproot is not how Opuntia is drawn in the comparators they cite, and there is one published identification rather than two.
